Explain the Question : A circular coil of n turns and radius r carries a current I. The magnetic field is measured on the axis of the coil at a small distance h from its centre. We have to find the fraction by which this field is smaller than the magnetic field at the centre.
Concept : This question is based on magnetic field on the axis of a circular current-carrying coil
Formula : Magnetic field on axis at distance x :
B(x) = (μ0 n I r2) / [2 (r2 + x2)3/2]
Magnetic field at centre :
B0 = (μ0 n I) / (2r)
Solution : Magnetic field at distance h from centre,
B(h) = (μ0 n I r2) / [2 (r2 + h2)3/2]
For h ≪ r,
(r2 + h2)3/2 ≈ r3 [1 + (3/2)(h2 / r2)]
So,
B(h) ≈ (μ0 n I / 2r) [1 − (3/2)(h2 / r2)]
Since B0 = μ0 n I / 2r,
Fractional decrease in field
(B0 − B(h)) / B0 = (3/2)(h2 / r2)
Final answer : 1

"

"Concept:

  • Boiling Point: Alcohols form intermolecular hydrogen bonds due to the  -OH  group; ethers cannot hydrogen bond with themselves, leading to lower boiling points.

  • Solubility: Both can form hydrogen bonds with water molecules, making their miscibility comparable.

Solution: 

  • Statement-I is incorrect: Ethers lack intermolecular hydrogen bonding; only alcohols have it. This disparity causes the boiling point difference.

  • Statement-II is correct: Both ethoxyethane and butan-1-ol (isomers,  C4H10O ) show similar solubility (approx. 7–9 g/100 mL) because both can accept hydrogen bonds from water.

Final Answer : Option (4)"
